findings.summary: read_resource performs no arity or non-empty check, so an empty caller and empty owner compare equal and the function returns the value with success status, authorizing unauthenticated access.

The digit regex is followed by an arithmetic range check, so values above 2^64 wrap around and are accepted as valid page sizes while leading-zero inputs like 08 are parsed as octal and fail with a bash error.

Every backend failure is swallowed and converted into an empty JSON array with exit status 0, making an unreachable store indistinguishable from an empty one and risking data loss in read-modify-write callers.
Locking and increment logic are correct, but non-numeric file content is silently coerced to 0, resetting the counter instead of reporting corruption.
JSON encoding is safe, but a missing argument silently yields an empty displayName instead of an error.
